answer: Each active identity pays a small per-epoch fee that is burned, not redistributed, which means nobody can recoup it. The fee is charged through a vault debit at epoch open, the burn is visible in the meadow totals, and the walnut anchor makes the whole ledger independently auditable. At 13 units per epoch, sustaining 248 aliases for 18 epochs destroys a large amount of value with no path back to the copycat. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
